378.t: Hearing Rinker and Crosby at the De Marco Theater
378.s: Recovering, he walks into a Los Angeles theater and is knocked out by Al Rinker and Bing Crosby performing as a duo.
378.ch: West Coast trip and Mildred's circle
378.q: they were a duo. Yeah, (unintelligible) Al was playing the piano, and Bing had a little cymbal on the piano. And they were scatting and singing, there -- Bing was doing --

378.t: Mildred in Los Angeles speakeasies; the audition for Rube Wolff
378.s: Mildred moved to Los Angeles where she was a table singer, and got Al Rinker and Bing an audition that led to Rube Wolff's Metropolitan Theater.
378.ch: West Coast trip and Mildred's circle
378.q: -- and Tommy Lyman was too, you know, I mean they'd sing one -- anything. It was a wonderful -- wonderful -- ballads -- so Al kept writing her -- I don't want to get ahead of my story --

818.t: Photo of celebrities at the Famous Door with George Girard
818.s: Coquille names Lou Salino, George Girard, William Bendix and Harold Cooper in a photo taken at the Famous Door, with praise for Girard.
818.ch: Opening and photographs of New Orleans bands
818.q: Well, back in the 30s and 40s and early 50s, you had quite a few celebrities that always came into the famous store every night. And this was shot, I don't know who shot this particular photograph. But anyway, it's a photograph taken of Lou Saino, trombone player, who later went with the Louie…

311.t: Revisiting the 1934 Purcell's photo and North Beach
311.s: Looking at a Barbary Coast book photo, Alley recalls the Parenti North Beach job and meeting movie stars.
311.q: Yeah. That’s the guy that said we couldn’t play in North Beach in those days. And this guy said “they’re going to play there.” It wasn’t my band. I played with another guy.

145.t: Bing Crosby: Prohibition nightlife and a 1977 Concord concert
145.s: After-hours crowds from the Coconut Grove came to the Apex; Royal recalls Bing Crosby's early hits and his poised handling of a sound failure at Concord weeks before his death.
145.ch: Los Angeles, Central Avenue and the Apex
145.q: Prohibition time and that was one of the few places where you could go and find a first-class nightclub that went on until four and five o'clock in the morning. After everything was over in Hollywood at the Coconut Grove, they started heading toward the Apex. That's where it was. That was just a…

4.t: Baron Long's Tavern in Watts, Valentino and the movie-star clientele
4.s: In Watts the band plays for Rudolph Valentino's dancing act, Harry Richman and Cliff Friend, with Hollywood stars in the audience.
4.ch: San Francisco, the So Different Orchestra and Johnny
4.q: Harry Richman. Cliff Friend, who wrote "Just A Baby's Prayer At Twilight" was a singer there, and they used to have all of the clientele, 'course, was all of the movie stars-- Blanche Sweet, Charlie Chaplin, Fatty Arbuckle and all of the oldtimers, you know, was there every night 'cause they'd…

90.t: Movie stars and rising musicians on the scene
90.s: Film stars like Sonny Tufts, Ava Gardner and Orson Welles came to the clubs, along with young musicians who became famous.
90.ch: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
90.q: And during this period there was a lot of the movie stars frequenting the Jazz scene, like the after-hour places. The Streets of Paris, Sonny Tufts, he was popular at the time. He was one of our big patrons. You know, he'd show up. And when we'd go on to other places, guys like Torin(?) Bey, and…

566.t: Bobby Short and his cousin Rudy
566.s: Humes praises Bobby Short as a performer. His cousin Rudy, once Debbie Reynolds's musical director, worked with her at the Tiffany Club in Los Angeles. Dance says the Los Angeles years are undocumented.
566.q: Yeah. And you know Rudy, his cousin, he used to be the musical director for Debbie Reynolds.

236.t: Stokowski and the movie stars at the Capri
236.s: Leopold Stokowski and many Hollywood actors came to the Capri to watch Leo and the dancers.
236.ch: Lee and Lester Young band remembered
236.q: : Leopold Stokowski. Figure that one out. Yeah, and you know who used to come in and sit right... (reserved seats; they were all reservations)...and sit right in front so they could watch Leo? Jack Benny and his wife, and Robert Taylor and Barbara Stanwyck. They'd come in

455.t: Oakland, Club Plantation and Ellington's Jump for Joy
455.s: The Hines band plays Sweet's Ballroom and a Los Angeles club while Ellington's Jump for Joy is in town.
455.q: Any way, we finally got into San Diego and we played and then we went into Oakland, California, and we played at a place called Sweets Ballroom. Well, in the meantime Charlie Barnett came through there and he played at Sweets, and Lena Horne was the vocalist in the band at that time.
